newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: PRESS DIGEST - Pakistani newspapers - May 29.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Pakistani newspapers - May 29.

text.p: These are the leading stories in the Pakistani press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
DAWN

- The State (central) Bank of Pakistan may ask the government to pay interest at market rates - higher than the yield on security papers - if the government borrows beyond the fixed target of 50 billion rupees set for fiscal 1997/98 (July-June).
- Pakistan's foreign ministry summoned the acting Indian High Commissioner and lodged a strong protest over the alleged violation of its airspace by an Indian fighter plane on May 27.

- Foreign Minister Gohar Ayub Khan said Islamabad was engaged in a detailed analysis of the violation of its airspace by an Indian aircraft but did not say if it could affect the forthcoming secretary-level talks between the two countries.
- Pakistan's economic growth during 1996/97 (July-June) would be at 2.7 percent, the state's Planning Commission said.

- Pakistan's population is projected to go up to 269 million by the year 2025 from 144 million at present and growing at an annual rate of 2.7 percent, the United Nation's State of the World Population report said.
- Finance Minister Sartaj Aziz said the rupee was not being devalued but was just being technically adjusted.
- Prime Minister Nawaz Sharif has approved a comprehensive plan for the complete privatisation of state-run Pakistan Railways within the next 30 months, sources said.

- Pakistan's central bank announced a five percent cut in the statutory reserves the banks are required to maintain with it. The move is expected to bring about 45 billion rupees in the financial system.
BUSINESS RECORDER
- The SBP has set a target of 145 billion rupees for domestic credit expansion.
- Pakistan Vanaspati Manufacturers Association has offered to reduce cooking oil prices if the government cuts import duty on soyabean oil.
- Finance Minister Sartaj Aziz said the revenue receipts during July-April were 221 billion rupees, which was only 65 percent of the total revenue target set in the 1996/97 budget.
THE NEWS
- Pakistan is considering a proposal to impose anti-dumping laws on the goods damaging local industry.
- Prime Minister Nawaz Sharif will set up accountability committees throughout the country.
THE NATION
- Indian war preparations have intensified along the line of control in Kashmir.
-- Islamabad newsroom 274757
